items.title: The module generated by a sequence with Koszul relations surjects onto the ideal with kernel annihilated by it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the naive Koszul module of a finitely generated ideal: the module M generated by elements e_1 to e_n subject to the relations f_i e_j = f_j e_i maps onto the ideal I generated by the f_i, and the kernel of that map is annihilated by I (statement lines 24393-24402). The proof is six lines (proof lines 24405-24410) and it consists of the definition of the map e_i to f_i together with one computation: for m = sum a_i e_i in the kernel, that is with sum a_i f_i = 0, one multiplies m by f_j, rewrites the result using the relations as the single term (sum f_i a_i) e_j, and concludes that it vanishes because of the relation sum a_i f_i = 0. The factorisation of the short exact sequence is therefore explicit, and the annihilation statement is checked on the generators of the kernel rather than only on M.
